children: Wall Street came under renewed pressure Tuesday as a jump in Treasury yields and higher oil prices added to investor caution before the Federal Reserve's policy decision.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 0.8%, while the S&P 500 slipped about 0.59%. The Nasdaq Composite declined about 0.7% as investors also assessed fresh concerns surrounding the outlook for artificial-intelligence spending.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield briefly climbed above 5%, reaching its highest level since 2007. Rising borrowing costs can weigh on equity valuations, particularly for companies whose expected growth is further out.
Energy stocks provided some support as crude prices remained above $100 a barrel amid supply concerns. Most other sectors traded lower.

Investors are now focused on Wednesday's Fed decision. Market pricing points to a quarter-point increase, which would mark the first rate hike since 2023. The move comes as policymakers face renewed inflation pressure from energy prices and elevated borrowing costs.

title: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Fall Ahead of Fed Decision
